summary:
## 🌟 Summary
Ultralytics **8.4.204** makes high-resolution tiling available across training, validation, and prediction, and adds improvements to FastSAM prompts, model exports, and dataset handling.

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🧩 **High-resolution tiling:** Use `tile=True` or a positive integer tile size to process large images in overlapping windows. Training crops labels to each tile; validation and prediction merge results back into the original image.
- 📚 **Updated tiling documentation and examples:** A new **High Resolution Tiling** guide covers usage, supported tasks, and performance considerations. The SAHI guide remains available with a deprecation notice directing users to the built-in `tile` option, and the video example now uses the standard YOLO CLI and Python API.
- 🎯 **Better FastSAM text prompts:** FastSAM now uses a DataComp-XL CLIP model that selects the correct mask more often, with similar speed and download size.
- ⚡ **Faster LiteRT quantization:** INT8 and w8a16 calibration now use a C++ profiling mode. In the reported benchmark, export time dropped from about 36 seconds to 11 seconds, with no measured validation accuracy regression.
- 🛠️ **More dependable exports and calibration:** INT8 calibration now supports NDJSON and Platform datasets. NCNN export reports models its runtime cannot load, and dependency fixes address issues affecting TensorFlow, RKNN, Axelera, and Xilinx exports.
- 🔧 **Additional fixes:** RT-DETR INT8 export avoids known failures on certain SM 12.1 GPUs; resumed training uses new augmentation randomness; and the YAML parser accepts spaces before the colon after quoted keys.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- 🐜 Tiling can preserve small-object detail in large images without requiring a separate tiling package. It works across several vision tasks, but increases the number of model passes and may take more time and memory.
- 🚀 Export and calibration changes can make deployment workflows faster or more reliable, particularly on affected hardware and formats.
- 📖 Users can use the built-in tiling option throughout training, evaluation, and prediction, while the existing SAHI guide remains accessible with a deprecation notice.
- 📦 The release updates the package version to **8.4.204**. The release PR primarily updates documentation and examples; the other merged PRs provide the additional runtime and export changes.

## What's Changed
* Keep RT-DETR INT8 squeeze convs and attention in float on SM 12.1 (GB10, N1X) by @atakann in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27049
* Use profiler-based calibration for faster LiteRT INT8 and w8a16 export by @amanharshx in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27062
* Accept spaces before the colon after quoted YAML keys by @MohammadHijjawi97 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27052
* Fail NCNN export when NCNN cannot load the converted model by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27056
* Use DataComp-XL CLIP ViT-B/32 for FastSAM text prompts by @Y-T-G in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27060
* Fix saving multispectral detection crops by @Vaishnavi220506 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27054
* Remove unused dataset YAML bash download route by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27065
* Reseed RNG on resume so resumed epochs do not replay earlier augmentations by @Y-T-G in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27064
* Reuse dataset conversion for INT8 calibration by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27067
* Fix dependency setup in TensorFlow, RKNN, Axelera and Xilinx exports by @Y-T-G in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26859
* Add high resolution tiling for all vision tasks by @Laughing-q in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27059
* Release 8.4.204 with High Resolution Tiling documentation by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27069


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.203...v8.4.204

summary:
RF-DETR 1.12.0 gives native and exported models one prediction API, adds INT8 exports, and speeds up inference on CUDA and Apple Silicon.

- Predict from images, folders, video files, cameras, and RTSP streams through one **RFDETRInference** API for native and exported models.
- Export INT8 engines for TensorRT, ONNX, and OpenVINO with `quantization="int8"`.
- Get faster default inference: CUDA graphs on CUDA, inductor on Apple silicon, and batches prepared while the last one runs.
- Set a confidence threshold per class with **ClassThresholds**.

Eight behavior changes need a look, mostly `RFDETR.inference()` returning a predictor and stricter Kornia training settings; see the Migration guide. Unknown `predict()` keywords and `TRTInference` are deprecated.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### One prediction API for native and exported models

`RFDETRInference` runs a live model, a native checkpoint or any supported export through the same preprocessing and decoding, and returns Supervision detections. It reads directories, globs, video files, cameras, RTSP and `.streams` manifests, and `stream=True` yields results as they arrive. (#1563, #1577)

```python
from rfdetr import RFDETRInference, RFDETRSmall

predictor = RFDETRSmall().inference()  # independent, compiled snapshot
detections = predictor.predict("image.jpg")

onnx = RFDETRInference("output/inference_model.onnx")
for result in onnx.predict("video.mp4", stream=True):
    ...
```

### Performance per hardware

`RFDETRSmall`, batch 1, end to end (preprocessing, forward, postprocessing) through `RFDETRInference` or the `inference()` snapshot. Compare within a row, not across machines.

| Hardware | Fastest route | Precision | Latency [ms] | FPS [img/s] |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA L4 | TensorRT `.trt` engine | fp16 | 3.57 | 280 |
| Apple M4 Max (40-core GPU) | `inference()` inductor | fp16 | 10.3 | 97.4 |
| x86 CPU (Colab, 4 cores / 8 threads) | OpenVINO IR | fp32 | 373.7 | 2.7 |

On the L4 the `inference()` CUDA graph in fp16 reaches 3.60 ms, level with the engine at batch 1. On the M4 Max `inference()` inductor in fp16 runs 10.3 ms against 20.0 ms for eager `predict()`. On x86 the run-to-run spread is 10 to 17% of the mean, so gaps under about 100 ms are noise. Results for NVIDIA T4, A100 and RTX PRO 6000 and for all four model sizes are in the "Measured Performance by Hardware" section of the export docs index; the mobile and edge CPU tables are pending a rerun.

### INT8 exports for TensorRT, ONNX and OpenVINO

`quantization="int8"` with `calibration_data` builds INT8 TensorRT engines for detection, segmentation and keypoint models, and static INT8 for ONNX and OpenVINO. On an RTX 5070 and a Tesla T4, TensorRT INT8 ran 1.08× to 1.41× faster than FP16 and was 25% to 39% smaller, at a cost of 0.27 to 1.01 AP points at batch 1. (#1595, #1627, #1560)

```python
model.export(format="tensorrt", quantization="int8", calibration_data="path/to/images", batch_size=8)
```

### Faster default inference

`RFDETR.inference()` now captures a CUDA graph on CUDA and compiles with inductor on MPS. CUDA prediction prepares the next batch while the current one runs and decodes baseline JPEG batches with nvjpeg. In one benchmark (L4, RF-DETR Nano, FP16, batch 1), CUDA graph replay cut median end-to-end latency from 9.719 ms to 3.884 ms with identical COCO AP. (#1547, #1668, #1670, #1672)

### Per-class confidence thresholds

Name the classes that need their own bar and give the rest a default. (#1635)

```python
from rfdetr import ClassThresholds

detections = model.predict(image, threshold=ClassThresholds({"person": 0.35, "traffic light": 0.6}, default=0.5))
```

### Smaller Plus models and a backbone registry

`RFDETRAtto`, `RFDETRFemto` and `RFDETRPico` ship through `rfdetr_plus` (`pip install "rfdetr[plus]"`, Platform Model License 1.0: commercial use is included when deploying on Roboflow, and commercial self-hosting needs the Enterprise add-on). `rfdetr.models.backbone.register_backbone` lets an extension package supply a non-DINOv2 encoder. (#1568)

## 🔄 Migration guide

Each change below failed or behaved differently on 1.11.x with no deprecation shim.

### `RFDETR.inference()` returns a predictor

The return value is now an independent `RFDETRInference`, and the `inplace` keyword is rejected. (#1563)

```python
# Before (1.11.x)
model.inference(compile=True, inplace=True)
detections = model.predict(image)

# After (1.12.0)
predictor = model.inference(compile=True)
detections = predictor.predict(image)
```

Each predictor owns a copy of the current base weights; delete it when you no longer need its runtime. The default compile backend now follows the device: a CUDA graph on CUDA, inductor on MPS, TorchScript elsewhere. Pass `compile_backend="torchscript"` for the previous default.

### Kornia training rejects padded batches

Detection and segmentation training with a Kornia-resolved `augmentation_backend` raises `ValueError` during setup when `square_resize_div_64=False` or `multi_scale="per-sample"`. (#1680)

```python
# After: pick one
model.train(..., square_resize_div_64=True, multi_scale="per-batch")  # or "off"
model.train(..., augmentation_backend="torchvision")  # or "albumentations"
```

### Kornia `Affine` configs

`Affine(translate_px=...)` is now applied; 1.11.2 ignored it. Combinations Kornia cannot reproduce (rotation, scale, shear, a nonzero fill, reflected borders) raise `ValueError` when the pipeline is built, so use `augmentation_backend="cpu"` (Albumentations, `rfdetr[augment]`) to keep them. (#1607)

An `Affine` config without `rotate` no longer rotates images; it used to sample a random ±15° rotation. Set `rotate=(-15, 15)` to keep the old behavior. The built-in presets are unaffected. (#1679)

### Core ML float16 outputs

`format="coreml"` with `coreml_precision="float16"` now returns float32 output arrays, because the `.mlpackage` is converted as an iOS 15 program. Read outputs as float32. `coreml_precision="float32"` bundles are unchanged. (#1604)

### `rfdetr[onnx]` drops `polygraphy` and `onnx_graphsurgeon`

A host that exports to TensorRT or TFLite with `rfdetr[onnx]` plus a separately installed `tensorrt` or `onnx2tf` must install the missing package itself. (#1589)

```bash
pip install polygraphy onnx_graphsurgeon
```

### Segmentation eval outputs

In eval mode, a segmentation `LWDETR` no longer returns `pred_masks` in `aux_outputs` or `enc_outputs`. Code that runs `SetCriterion` on eval-mode outputs must pass `all_layer_masks=True`; the final `pred_masks` are unchanged. (#1628)

### `RFDETR.export(batch_size=...)` is validated first

`batch_size` must be an integer. A `bool`, `2.0`, `"2"` or `None` now raises `ValueError` before the forward pass; a `bool` used to export batch size 1. (#1556)

### Deprecations and removals to act on

- Unknown keyword arguments to `RFDETR.predict()` are ignored with a `FutureWarning` and will raise `TypeError` in v2.0.0. `stream`, `batch`, `vid_stride` and `stream_buffer` raise `TypeError` now; use `RFDETRInference` for them. (#1563, #1577)
- `TRTInference` and `OpenVINOInference` are deprecated and scheduled for removal in v1.15.0. Use `RFDETRInference` on the exported artifact. `OpenVINOInference` now defaults `inference_precision` to `"f32"` on every device except NPU; pass `inference_precision=None` to restore the device default.
- The `rfdetr.datasets.aug_config` module is removed after deprecation since v1.9.0. Import the presets from `rfdetr.datasets.aug_configs`. (#1662)

## 📝 Notable changes

### 🚀 Added

- **Unified inference** — public `RFDETRInference`, versioned export metadata (embedded in ONNX, `<artifact>.rfdetr.json` sidecars elsewhere), `RFDETR.write_export_metadata` for older exports, and `runtime_options` for per-format runtime settings. (#1563)
- **Streaming and expanded inputs** — `RFDETRInference.predict()` reads videos, directories, globs, CSV and `.streams` manifests, cameras, RTSP and HTTP live sources, YouTube and the screen, with `stream`, `batch`, `vid_stride` and `stream_buffer`; `RFDETR.predict()` accepts any iterable of images and a BCHW tensor as one batch. New `rfdetr[stream]` extra. (#1577)
- **Per-class thresholds** — `predict(threshold=ClassThresholds(...))`. (#1635)
- **TensorRT** — INT8 engines for detection, segmentation and keypoint models with SmoothQuant and MLP bias correction on detection; `trt_metadata=True` writes an `<engine>.json` description; `trt_hardware_compatibility` and `trt_version_compatible` build engines other GPUs or TensorRT releases can load; `trt_timing_cache` reuses kernel timings; `TRTInference(cuda_graph=True)` replays the launch from a CUDA graph. (#1595, #1627, #1638, #1642, #1645, #1581, #1580, #1579, #1583)
- **Static INT8 for ONNX and OpenVINO** with `quantization="int8"` and `calibration_data`. (#1560)
- **Core ML** — `notes` and the RF-DETR version stored in `.mlpackage` metadata; `coreml_neural_engine=True` moves the model onto the Neural Engine (`resample` and `cast` still run on the CPU). (#1609, #1586)
- **Runtime helpers** — public `rfdetr.export.inference` (`TRTInference`, `load_executorch_method`, `preprocess_to_nchw`, `decode_detections`, `DecodedDetections`) and `rfdetr.export.benchmark` (`measure_latency`, `measure_memory`). (#1585)
- **`RFDETR.inference(compile_backend="cudagraph")`** — direct CUDA Graph replay for fixed batch size and resolution. (#1547)
- **Plus models and backbones** — `RFDETRAtto`, `RFDETRFemto`, `RFDETRPico`; `register_backbone`; `ModelConfig.dim_feedforward`; `RFDETRModelModule(load_encoder_weights=False)`. (#1568)
- **Training** — Kornia augmentation for keypoints (#1606); `eval_backend="hotcoco_streaming"` (#1590, #1614); `build_trainer(extra_callbacks=[...])` (#1629).
- **`RFDETR.predict(antialias=...)`** — opt-in antialiased resizing. (#1525)

### ⚠️ Breaking Changes

- **Kornia training** — padded batches (`square_resize_div_64=False`, `multi_scale="per-sample"`) raise `ValueError`. Use `square_resize_div_64=True` with `multi_scale="per-batch"` or `"off"`, or `augmentation_backend="torchvision"` or `"albumentations"`. (#1680)
- **`RFDETR.inference()`** — returns an independent `RFDETRInference`; `inplace` is removed. Capture the return value and call `predictor.predict(...)`; pass `compile_backend="torchscript"` for the previous default backend. (#1563)
- **Core ML** — float16 bundles return float32 outputs. Read float32, or cast with `astype(np.float16)`. (#1604)
- **`rfdetr[onnx]`** — no longer installs `polygraphy` or `onnx_graphsurgeon`. Run `pip install polygraphy onnx_graphsurgeon` for TensorRT or TFLite exports. (#1589)
- **Kornia `Affine`** — `translate_px` is applied, unsupported combinations raise, and an unset `rotate` no longer rotates. Use `augmentation_backend="cpu"` for unsupported combinations, and set `rotate=(-15, 15)` for the old rotation. (#1607, #1679)
- **Segmentation eval** — no `pred_masks` in auxiliary outputs unless `all_layer_masks=True`. Pass it when you compute a loss on eval-mode outputs. (#1628)
- **`export(batch_size=...)`** — non-integer values raise `ValueError`. Pass a positive integer such as `batch_size=1`. (#1556)

### 🌱 Changed

- **Faster inference defaults** — CUDA `inference()` captures a CUDA graph; MPS compiles with inductor, fuses `F.grid_sample` (and folds LayerScale unless the inductor backend is used); CUDA prediction on an owned model prepares the next batch ahead; baseline JPEG batches decode with nvjpeg; ONNX Runtime on CUDA preprocesses on the GPU with IO binding. (#1672, #1668, #1666, #1670)
- **Batching** — `predict()` without `batch` runs a directory or glob in batches of eight on models without a fixed batch size and on dynamic-batch exports; pass `batch=1` for the previous results. (#1664, #1672)
- **Host copies** — non-CUDA accelerators copy boxes, scores and labels once per batch. (#1664, #1668)
- **Training speed** — Triton-fused clip, AdamW and EMA for single-GPU compiled BF16 (#1529); `vernier>=0.6.0` as the default eval backend (#1661); GPU RLE encoding of segmentation masks (#1615); last-layer-only masks in segmentation eval (#1628); depthwise convolutions use cuDNN on compute capability 8.0 and newer (#1513); the progress bar shows the running mean of loss terms (#1625).
- **Dependencies** — `hotcoco>=1.2.1,<1.3`, `rfdetr_plus>=1.1.0`, `ultrafast-pycocotools>=0.1.13`. (#1590, #1614, #1568, #1584)
- **Export** — arguments and packages are checked before the forward pass; LiteRT samples deformable attention from pixel rows; ExecuTorch XNNPACK keeps attention in the delegate; TensorRT refuses a non-int8 `quantization` or stray `calibration_data`. (#1556, #1587, #1601, #1595)
- **Weights** — pretrained weights download from `repo.roboflow.com/rfdetr`. (#1600)
- **Deprecated-model warnings** now name the replacement class. (#1618)

### 🗑️ Deprecated

- Unknown keyword arguments to `RFDETR.predict()`; removal as `TypeError` in v2.0.0. (#1563)
- `TRTInference` and `OpenVINOInference`; removed in v1.15.0. (#1563)

### ❌ Removed

- `rfdetr.datasets.aug_config`, deprecated since v1.9.0. Import from `rfdetr.datasets.aug_configs`. (#1662)
- `onnxsim`, `onnx_graphsurgeon` and `polygraphy` from the `[onnx]` extra, and `polygraphy` and `onnxsim` from `[tflite]`. (#1589, #1563)
- The private `OnnxOptimizer`, `onnx_simplify` and `_onnx.symbolic` modules. (#1589)

### 🔧 Fixed

- Prediction: keypoint `covariance` on frames with no detections (#1681); bfloat16 tensors as source images (#1682); `inference()` on CUDA segmentation models under deterministic mode (#1673); keypoint scores in fp16 and bf16 (#1632).
- Training and checkpoints: `from_checkpoint("run.pth")` loads the file it was given (#1683); a checkpoint-derived `num_classes` no longer blocks dataset alignment (#1674); resuming applies a changed `lr` or `weight_decay` (#1619); `BestModelCallback` honors the Lightning checkpoint lifecycle (#1678); an invalid `better` in `BestMetricSingle` raises `ValueError` (#1608).
- Augmentation: segmentation boxes follow the transformed masks and empty masks are dropped (#1658); Kornia keeps continuous box edges (#1621); torchvision keypoint flips use continuous coordinates (#1597).
- Export: `tflite` converts with onnx2tf 2.4.3 on a fresh install (#1563); Core ML segmentation masks line up on the Neural Engine (#1657); FP16 sigmoid in the shared export decoder (#1648); `output_name` keeps dots (#1641); metadata type checking no longer fails on Windows (#1640).
- Evaluation and data: mixed keypoint-count mAP and mAR (#1686); COCO polygon parts with fewer than three points are skipped (#1644); per-class table class names print verbatim (#1598); `evaluate()` no longer downloads encoder weights (#1568).
- Loading: no DINOv2 skip warnings on pretrained load (#1653); the class-count warning wording is clearer (#1654); a TorchScript error falls back to eager losses (#1649); the CLI parses the shipped configs and builds the trainer (#1629); the sine-embedding frequencies build in float32 for half-precision Inductor compiles (#1616).

## 🏆 Contributors

- **Lương Thanh Hoàng Phú** (@lthphuw, [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/in/phu-lth)) — built INT8 TensorRT engines for detection, segmentation and keypoint models with `quantization="int8"`; added hardware- and version-compatible TensorRT engines, CUDA-graph launch replay and kernel-timing reuse; added one `threshold` per class in `predict`.
- **Lee Clement** (@leeclemnet, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/leeclemnet)) — unified native and exported model prediction behind one inference path; expanded prediction inputs and added streaming; added `coreml_neural_engine` to run Core ML exports fully on the Neural Engine.
- **Jesús Royeth** (@JESUSROYETH, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jesusroyeth/)) — added direct CUDA Graph replay for inference; fused AdamW and EMA updates with Triton; added Kornia augmentation support for keypoints.
- **Raghav Rathi** (@raghav-rathi, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/raghavrathi00/)) — encoded segmentation masks to COCO RLE on the GPU; computed only the last decoder layer's masks in segmentation models; fixed the CLI to parse the shipped configs and build the trainer correctly.
- **Barsam Ershadi** (@BarsamErshadi, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/barsam-ershadi/)) — fixed `from_checkpoint` to load weights from the file it was given; fixed bfloat16 source images and keypoint covariance on empty frames in prediction; rejected padded Kornia batches for every model.
- **Luís Condados** (@Gabriellgpc, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/luis-condados)) — sped up the RF-DETR-Seg training step.
- **Matvei Popov** (@Matvezy, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/matvezy)) — added a backbone registry and Plus model exports for the smaller RF-DETR sizes.
- **Erle Carrara** (@ecarrara) — switched pretrained weight downloads to the Roboflow repository; cached pretrained weights across CI jobs.
- **Tamil Adhavan S K** (@adhavan18, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tamiladhavan)) — added opt-in antialiased resizing in `predict`.
- **Yonghye Kwon** (@developer0hye, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yonghye-kwon-91641a174/)) — sped up `ufcoco` evaluation by loading box-only detections from one array.
- **Noé Fontana** (@NoeFontana, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/noe-fontana/)) — moved training to vernier 0.6 for faster evaluation.
- **Vlad Voropaev** (@voropaevv, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/thevladvoropaev/)) — made `BestModelCallback` honor the Lightning checkpoint lifecycle; added MPS threshold and output-alignment test coverage.
